memory_update.text: SPSC maps most directly to the Consumer retail-infrastructure chokepoint through retail trading-partner networks, EDI/API order exchange, supplier connectivity, vendor compliance, and recurring network workflows.

TRAK should remain in the speculative_shadow lane: possible grocery traceability and FSMA 204 supplier-network beneficiary, but evidence must prove durable recurring revenue, network effects, and customer adoption beyond regulatory deadline pull-forward.

DSGX maps to a broader logistics-network and trade-compliance node with possible hidden retail and consumer-commerce exposure through B2B Integration, EDI Messaging, customs, routing, and ecommerce logistics workflows.

OTEX maps to a broader enterprise software company with a potentially valuable but diluted B2B integration and Trading Grid exposure; the key question is whether Business Network is material to consolidated OpenText growth and margins.

BILL is not yet a confirmed Consumer supply-chain chokepoint; retain only as a speculative payments and remittance-data adjacency until filings or customer evidence show retail, CPG, supplier-network, or compliance-workflow materiality.

MANH and ORCL should be used as reference benchmarks and platform-displacement tests, not underfollowed candidates, because their company-level narratives are already well followed and their exposure is broader than the candidate chokepoint.

Need current market-pricing checks for all tickers: market cap, valuation, revenue-growth expectations, analyst count, liquidity, short interest, institutional ownership, and whether retail-infrastructure exposure is already priced.

Need primary-source evidence for customer concentration, named retailer or supplier relationships, retention, transaction volume, partner count, and revenue by product or vertical for SPSC, TRAK, DSGX, OTEX, BILL, MANH, and ORCL.

Need falsification work on whether ERP, WMS, OMS, procurement, and cloud application suites are displacing specialist retail EDI networks or coexisting with them through integrations and partner ecosystems.

Need to expand Layer 2B beyond this candidate chunk into reverse logistics, returns/recommerce, testing and certification, labeling, customs brokerage, merchant acquiring, loyalty, gift-card infrastructure, and travel operating systems.

summary: Layer 2B maps the candidate chunk into ticker-level relationships around a narrower Consumer infrastructure chokepoint: retail trading-partner networks, EDI/API order exchange, supplier compliance, grocery traceability, logistics connectivity, and adjacent supplier-payment workflows. The strongest mapped relationship remains SPSC as the clearest pure-play retail trading-partner network. TRAK is retained as a speculative micro-cap FSMA 204 and grocery traceability network candidate. DSGX and OTEX are broader infrastructure companies where consumer-retail exposure may be hidden inside logistics, B2B integration, trade compliance, and EDI network segments. BILL remains a weakly supported speculative adjacency rather than a confirmed retail supplier-network asset. MANH and ORCL are reference comparables for warehouse, omnichannel, ERP, and platform competition, not primary underfollowed alpha candidates. No buy/sell recommendation is made; this output is for research tracking and evidence planning only.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether gross retention, net revenue retention, transaction volume, retailer/supplier logo additions, and compliance-workflow adoption show that the network is deepening despite slower supplier technology spending.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull latest SPSC 10-K, 10-Q, investor deck, and earnings-call transcript; extract recurring revenue mix, customer count, revenue growth by solution, retention commentary, retailer/supplier additions, and any tariff or macro-delay commentary.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Pure-play retail supply-chain network connecting retailers, suppliers, distributors, grocers, manufacturers, and logistics participants through recurring EDI/API, fulfillment, compliance, analytics, and trading-partner workflows.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether compliance-related modules are growing faster than core EDI document exchange and whether customers cite chargeback reduction or retailer mandate compliance as purchase drivers.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Search SPSC product pages, case studies, customer testimonials, and SEC filings for compliance, chargeback, vendor scorecard, fulfillment, routing guide, and analytics language.
ticker_relationships.relationship: SPSC may benefit when retailers increase supplier compliance requirements, vendor scorecards, fulfillment rules, routing-guide enforcement, and chargeback avoidance workflows because these raise the operational cost of weak supplier connectivity.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether customers are moving from simple EDI connectivity into API, automation, analytics, and multi-workflow orchestration, preserving SPSC relevance as retailer integration models modernize.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify product evolution from SPSC public filings and product material; compare against Oracle, Microsoft, SAP, Shopify, and large EDI/B2B integration providers to assess displacement risk.
ticker_relationships.relationship: SPSC appears to sit on the transaction rails between large retailers and suppliers; its potential chokepoint comes from retailer-specific integration maps, document rules, compliance logic, and supplier onboarding workflows built over many years.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether FSMA 204-driven onboarding converts into durable recurring SaaS revenue and multi-customer network effects, or whether adoption stalls after regulatory deadlines and suppliers resist fees.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull TRAK 10-K, 10-Q, earnings calls, customer announcements, FSMA 204 product disclosures, pricing structure, customer-count growth, churn, revenue-recognition policy, and related-party or concentration risks.
ticker_relationships.relationship: ReposiTrak is a speculative micro-cap candidate for grocery traceability, supplier onboarding, and FDA FSMA 204 compliance workflows; the possible chokepoint is a network of retailers, wholesalers, and food suppliers that need standardized traceability records.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether retailers or wholesalers pull suppliers onto the platform in a way that creates repeatable onboarding economics and cross-customer network effects.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Look for named retailer, wholesaler, and supplier rollouts; quantify supplier additions per quarter; identify whether onboarding is customer-funded, supplier-funded, or implementation-heavy.
ticker_relationships.relationship: TRAK may act as a supplier onboarding and compliance data layer for grocers and food distributors, but evidence is not yet strong enough to classify it as a durable trading-partner network rather than a narrow regulatory software vendor.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: How much revenue and growth are tied specifically to retail/wholesale EDI, supplier connectivity, and consumer-commerce logistics versus customs, routing, freight visibility, and other logistics modules.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review latest DSGX annual report and management commentary for Global Logistics Network, B2B Connectivity, EDI Messaging, ecommerce, retail, customs, and trade-compliance revenue drivers.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Descartes is a broader logistics network and trade-compliance software company with second-order consumer exposure through retailers, distributors, manufacturers, ecommerce firms, carriers, customs participants, and logistics service providers.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether trade-compliance module bookings, customer additions, and M&A commentary accelerate during periods of tariff volatility and customs enforcement.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track DSGX earnings transcripts for tariff, customs, sanctions, denied-party screening, ecommerce, de minimis, and forced-labor compliance references; compare organic growth versus acquisition contribution.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Descartes may benefit from tariff volatility, customs enforcement, country-of-origin documentation, forced-labor compliance, and cross-border ecommerce complexity because these increase demand for trade-compliance data and logistics connectivity.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether B2B integration and EDI messaging are material enough to create a distinct retail trading-partner network thesis within consolidated Descartes.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Use Descartes product documentation and filings to map B2B Integration customers, verticals, partner-count metrics, transaction metrics, and contribution to recurring revenue.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Descartes' B2B Integration and EDI Messaging products appear relevant to retail and supplier connectivity, but the company is less pure-play than SPSC and requires segment-level validation.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Business Network growth, margins, retention, transaction volumes, and retail/CPG customer mix are material enough to matter for consolidated OpenText.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Pull OpenText filings, investor presentations, and segment commentary; isolate Business Network revenue, cloud ARR, organic growth, profitability, customer mix, and retail or CPG references.
ticker_relationships.relationship: OpenText has a Business Network and Trading Grid asset that supports EDI, API, file-based, and ERP-integrated business exchange across retailers, manufacturers, logistics providers, banks, and other counterparties.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether OpenText is gaining, losing, or merely maintaining share in retail and CPG EDI networks while broader enterprise information-management segments dilute investor focus.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Compare OpenText Business Network disclosures with SPSC and DSGX on partner counts, transaction volumes, customer references, organic growth, and vertical specialization.
ticker_relationships.relationship: OpenText's Trading Grid may represent a large incumbent B2B document-exchange network that competes with or complements retail-focused specialists such as SPSC and logistics-network providers such as DSGX.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether enterprise-supplier and retail/consumer-brand use cases are material, recurring, and embedded enough to create network stickiness rather than commoditized payment processing.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review BILL filings and customer materials for vertical mix, supplier network metrics, enterprise AP/AR use cases, consumer-brand customers, retail customer examples, payment volume by vertical, and retention.
ticker_relationships.relationship: BILL is a speculative adjacency to the retail supplier-connectivity theme through AP, AR, payments, remittance data, and fragmented back-office workflows, but direct evidence of retail trading-partner compliance exposure is weak.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether BILL has any privileged role in supplier onboarding, invoice compliance, remittance reconciliation, or payment workflows for retail, CPG, hospitality, restaurants, or ecommerce sellers.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Search for named retail, restaurant, ecommerce, marketplace, franchise, CPG, or supplier-network customers; quantify how much revenue is from payments versus SaaS workflow automation.
ticker_relationships.relationship: BILL may benefit from consumer SMB digitization and supplier payment automation, but the relationship is currently too broad and generic for a Serenity chokepoint unless tied to durable supplier-network data or workflows.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Determine whether supplier enablement is a meaningful revenue driver or mainly a feature supporting broader WMS, OMS, transportation, and omnichannel deployments.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review MANH filings, product documentation, and earnings calls for supplier enablement, vendor collaboration, retailer integrations, EDI partnerships, and revenue contribution by product family.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Manhattan Associates is a reference leader in supply-chain execution, warehouse management, transportation, order management, omnichannel fulfillment, and retail operations software.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether retailers treat MANH as a system of execution that coexists with EDI networks, or whether MANH increasingly absorbs partner onboarding and compliance workflows.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Compare MANH implementation architecture with SPSC, DSGX, OTEX, Oracle, and large ERP systems; identify integrations and customer overlap.
ticker_relationships.relationship: MANH helps benchmark how much of the consumer supply-chain opportunity accrues to execution-system vendors versus specialist trading-partner networks.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether Oracle's integrated application suite is displacing specialist retail EDI networks or mostly coexisting with them through partner ecosystems and external EDI providers.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Review Oracle supply-chain, procurement, retail, and business-network product materials; search implementation partners and customer case studies for SPSC, OpenText, Descartes, and EDI coexistence.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Oracle is a mega-cap platform reference for ERP, cloud applications, retail, supply-chain planning, procurement, and business network functionality; it is included to test platform-displacement risk for specialist networks.

ticker_relationships.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether large retailers and suppliers prefer end-to-end ERP/application-suite connectivity or continue using specialist networks for trading-partner maps and compliance logic.
ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track customer win/loss evidence, partner listings, integration guides, analyst calls, and procurement case studies comparing Oracle-native workflows with specialist EDI/B2B integration vendors.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Oracle creates a key falsification path for the specialist network thesis: if large ERP and application platforms internalize EDI/API exchange, supplier onboarding, compliance, and data orchestration, smaller networks could face commoditization.
